exact_external_premises: For every integer d≥1, every connected open set Ω⊂C^d, and every plurisubharmonic function v on Ω that is not identically −∞, one has v∈L^1_loc(Ω). In particular {v=−∞} has Lebesgue measure zero. Consequently, a subset of a complex manifold that is locally contained in such −∞ loci has zero outer measure for every smooth volume measure.

source_reports.report: Demailly’s Chapter I, (5.3) and Theorem (4.17), establish local integrability with the stated connectedness and non-identically −∞ hypotheses. Local integrability makes the −∞ locus Lebesgue-null. Smooth volume is locally absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure; a countable coordinate subcover therefore gives zero outer measure even for arbitrary subsets of these loci. This verifies the exact supplied premise and its application to the smooth defect measure in part E.

root_math_assessment: Positive carrier-power bounds and Gauduchon trace control isolate intermediate closed currents and their zero complementary pairings. The Hopf horizontal coefficient and vertical Fourier argument forces base-measure pullback. Invariant averaging controls positive nonlinear cross terms at actual potential level, including the arbitrary orbital-law approximation. Curvature repair of linear automorphism pullbacks, exact standard quadratic mass adjustment and two independent diagonal selections realize every positive base measure. For arbitrary Hermitian metrics on the same manifold, repaired carrier currents and the explicit quadratic-plus-linear root give admissibility, exact mass and the complete weak measure limit. The pluripolarity equivalence follows from nontrivial psh fiber averages and countable fiber integration. General-manifold sufficiency is not proved.
root_editorial_expansion: The reverse outer-measure implication is expanded directly from both root-read complete independent n7 proofs. The full arbitrary-metric proof includes the quadratic-plus-linear mass correction; the scaled logarithmic global Omega-psh witness is a direct checked metric-comparison consequence. No private support-growth or heat-profile theorem is added.
